## TL;DR

Added a **Hide Completed Stories** control to the Stories page header (#1016).
It is a view-level filter over the already-derived story roll-up: when checked,
stories whose every member task is `done` disappear; when unchecked the full
list returns instantly, with no reload. The toggle defaults to **off**, so a
first load behaves exactly as before, and the choice persists per browser via
the repo store, like the page's sort order. Ordering and the sort control are
untouched because the filter runs after sorting. The change also adds an "All
stories are complete" empty state and tests for the toggle, the empty state,
persistence, and the no-tasks registered story.

## Work and rationale

The task was small and well-specified, so the work was mostly finding the right
place for the filter rather than writing novel logic.

**Where it lives.** `StoriesView.vue` already computes `stories` by merging
registered definitions with task roll-ups and then sorting. I added a
`visibleStories` computed wrapping the sorted list that, when the toggle is on,
drops groups with `complete === true`. `complete` is not new: it is the
existing derived flag in `src/core/stories.ts` meaning "every member task is
done", so no status or model changed. Filtering after `sortStoryGroupsForPage`
makes ordering provably unchanged when the toggle is off — the filter can only
remove rows, never reorder them.

**State and persistence.** The task said the toggle need not persist unless
trivial with an existing pattern; it was, so I persisted it. The repo store
already reads and writes `repoos.storiesPage.sortOrder` to `localStorage`, so I
added a parallel `storiesPageHideCompleted` ref, a reader defaulting to
`false`, and a setter storing `repoos.storiesPage.hideCompleted`. A user who
turns the filter on keeps it on across reloads; a first load still shows
everything.

**Markup and styling.** The control uses the shared
`components/ui/checkbox.vue` (Radix, styled), not a raw `<input>`. I wrapped it
in a `.stories-filter-toggle` label with the text "Hide Completed Stories". A
`<label>`'s labeled control may be a `<button>` (which is what Radix renders),
so clicking the text toggles it too — the same pattern the Inputs page uses.
The scoped styles mirror those filter chips (`inline-flex`, 7px gap,
`--txt-secondary`, pointer cursor) so list filters read consistently. It sits
in the existing header toolbar beside the sort dropdown and **New story**,
inside the `v-if="enabled"` block.

**Empty state.** The template showed "No stories yet" only for an empty
roll-up. With the filter on, `stories` can be non-empty while every story is
complete, which would render an empty grid with no explanation. I added a middle
branch: when `stories.length > 0` but `visibleStories.length === 0`, the page
shows "All stories are complete", the hidden count, and a pointer to uncheck the
toggle.

**Tests.** `stories-view.test.ts` gains a block covering the labelled control
and default ordering; hiding on check and restoring on uncheck via the rendered
`button[role='checkbox']`; persistence through the store and `localStorage`; the
completed-only empty state; and a registered story with zero tasks staying
visible because it is not complete. `repo-sort-order.test.ts` gained a
store-level default/persistence test. `user-docs/configuration.md` documents the
toggle, its default, persistence, and the no-tasks case.

## Approaches tried

- **`stories` vs a separate `visibleStories`.** I kept `stories` unfiltered and
  introduced `visibleStories` rather than mutating `stories`. This matters for
  the `?story=` deep link and the open side panel: both read `stories`, so a
  link to a completed story still opens its panel while the list is filtered —
  mirroring how `InputsView` lets a filtered-out input open.
- **`v-model:checked` on a writable computed.** I first wired
  `:checked`/`@update:checked` directly to the store, then switched to a
  writable `hideCompleted` computed with `v-model:checked`. Both work; the
  computed keeps the template declarative and puts the get/set persistence in
  one place.
- **Count beside the toggle vs only in the empty state.** I left the number out
  of the header to keep it quiet; the count appears where it explains what
  happened.
- **Persisting vs defaulting fresh.** Persistence was the only real design
  choice; defaulting to off preserves prior behaviour, which the acceptance
  criteria require when the toggle is off.

## Challenges and blockers

No human step and no external dependency. Two mechanical issues slowed things:

- Running the two test files with a bare `bunx vitest run` failed with "Install
  @vitejs/plugin-vue" and `localStorage is not defined`. That is the wrong
  config: UI tests need `--config src/ui-app/vite.config.ts` (which `bun run
  test` supplies). With the config, all 42 tests passed.
- The first `repoos check` failed `oxfmt --check` on `StoriesView.vue`;
  `bun run fmt` fixed it and the rerun passed. The self-check created the usual
  WIP checkpoint commits, so no source logic changed between runs.
- Finalizing the handoff then failed because this report was 1202 words against
  the 1,200 cap; I trimmed it and requested handoff again.

## Key learnings

- **"Completed" already existed and was derived.** `StoryGroup.complete` is
  "all member tasks done", so the feature is a filter over an existing boolean —
  no schema, route, or API change.
- **Order of composition is the correctness argument.** Filtering after the sort
  is what makes "ordering unchanged when off" obviously true.
- **Keep the deep-link path off the filtered list.** `findStoryByRef` and
  `openStory` still read unfiltered `stories`, so filtering never breaks a
  shared link to a finished story.
- **Persisting is cheap when a sibling pattern exists.** The sort-order
  localStorage reader/writer was an exact template.
- **The empty state is part of the feature.** A filter that can empty a
  populated list owes the user an explanation and a way back.
